chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Basir from Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

I went out with my father (peace be upon him) until we were between the grave [of the Prophet] and the pulpit, and he encountered people from the Shi'a. He gave them his salaam and they returned his salaam. Then he said: By Allah, I love your fragrance and your spirits, so support me in this through piety and striving. Know that our wilaya can only be reached through good deeds and striving. Whoever among you follows a servant [of God], let him act by his deeds.

You are the Shi'a of Allah and you are the supporters of Allah. You are the forerunners of the former and the latter peoples — the forerunners in this world toward our wilaya, and the forerunners in the Hereafter toward Paradise. We have guaranteed you Paradise with the guarantee of Allah and His Messenger. None among the ranks of Paradise has more spouses than you, so compete with one another in attaining the higher ranks. You are the pure ones, and your women are the pure ones. Every believing woman is a bright-eyed houri, and every believing man is a truthful one (siddiq).

And indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to Qanbar: 'O Qanbar! Rejoice, give glad tidings, and be joyful, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) died while he was displeased with his community — except the Shi'a.' Beware! For everything there is a firm handle, and the firm handle of Islam is the Shi'a. Beware! For everything there is a pillar, and the pillar of Islam is the Shi'a. Beware! For everything there is a nobility, and the nobility of Islam is the Shi'a. Beware! For everything there is a master, and the master of gatherings are the gatherings of the Shi'a. Beware! For everything there is an Imam, and the Imam of the earth is the land inhabited by the Shi'a.

By Allah, were it not for what of you is upon the earth, Allah would not have bestowed His blessings upon those who oppose you, nor would they have obtained good things. They have no share in this world or in the Hereafter. Every Nasib [opponent of the Ahlulbayt] — even if he worships and strives — is ascribed to this verse:

'Overburdened and exhausted, they will burn in a raging fire, left to drink from a scalding spring. They will have no food except a thorny shrub, neither nourishing nor satiating them from hunger.' [88:3-7]

Every striving Nasib, his deeds are in vain (haba'). Our Shi'a see by the light of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and those who oppose them stumble in the wrath of Allah. By Allah, there is not one servant from our Shi'a who sleeps except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, raises his spirit to heaven. If his appointed time has come, He places him in the treasuries of His mercy, in the gardens of His Paradise, and in the shade of His Throne. If his appointed time is yet to come, He sends him back with His trusted one among the angels to restore him to the body from which he came out, so that he may dwell in it. By Allah, your pilgrims of Hajj and 'Umra are the elect of Allah. Your poor ones are truly the wealthy, and your wealthy ones are truly the contented. And surely all of you are among those whom Allah has called and those who answered His call.

key_terms.الشِّيعَة: Shia — the followers/partisans of the Ahlulbayt; here used in the theological sense as the elect community
key_terms.صِدِّيق: Siddiq — the highest rank of truthful sainthood, below prophets
key_terms.عُرْوَة: Urwa — firm handle or handhold, as in the Quranic phrase 'the firmest handhold' (2:256)
key_terms.نَاصِب: Nasib — one who bears enmity toward the Ahlulbayt of the Prophet; their deeds are declared null
key_terms.هَبَاء: Haba' — dust scattered in the air; used metaphorically for deeds that count for nothing
key_terms.وَلَايَة: Wilaya — the spiritual authority and guardianship of the Ahlulbayt, loyalty to whom is a pillar of Shia faith

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say to the Shi'a between the Prophet's grave and pulpit?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrating an incident where his father, Imam al-Baqir (AS), encountered a group of Shi'a followers between the Prophet's grave and pulpit in Medina, and delivered a powerful exhortation extolling their spiritual status. The Imam declares that wilaya (guardianship of the Ahlulbayt) can only be attained through righteous deeds and piety, and assures the Shi'a of guaranteed Paradise with divine warranty. The hadith includes an embedded quote from Imam Ali (AS) to his servant Qanbar, a sustained rhetorical series declaring the Shi'a as the handle, pillar, nobility, and Imam of Islam, a citation of Quran 88:3-7 against opponents of the Ahlulbayt, and eschatological teachings about the elevation of Shi'a souls during sleep.
